newsitem.title: ITALY: Tietmeyer repeats need to respect EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer repeats need to respect EMU criteria.

text.p: Bundesbank chairman Hans Tietmeyer was quoted on Friday as saying that the decision on which countries will qualify for Europe's planned single currency would be taken without discrimination or privileges.

In an interview with the Italian newspaper Avvenire, he repeated that sustainable respect for the economic criteria required for membership of monetary and economic union (EMU) was the condition that counted.

The newspaper read his remarks as a signal that Italy still had a chance to qualify despite this week's European Commission forecast that its 1997 budget deficit was running at 3.2 percent of Gross Domestic Product -- above the 3.0 percent level required for EMU entry from January 1, 1999.
"I have said several times that all countries have the same rights to enter if they fully respect the criteria and if they are prepared to live in the euro zone for a long period," Tietmeyer said.

"That is precisely the point and that has to be verified next year but not now. Every country has a chance of getting in. There is no discrimination and there aren't any privileges for any countries, neither for Germany nor for others," he said.
